summary:
FireLens is a global web application that turns NASA FIRMS hotspot detections into an interactive map and a weekly fire activity calendar. Users can draw or select an area anywhere in the world to explore available records dating back to 2000, compare activity across years, and identify unusual weeks and seasonal peaks.

MODIS and VIIRS detect hotspots at different spatial resolutions, so a change in sensor can look like a change in fire activity. FireLens uses overlapping records from 2012 to 2021 to calibrate MODIS against VIIRS Suomi NPP by area and month. The harmonized calendar clearly distinguishes observed values from estimates, while the map displays observed satellite detections.

By putting recent detections in historical context, FireLens helps researchers and land managers see when activity typically peaks in an area and identify unusual periods that warrant closer investigation.
details:
FireLens is a global web application for exploring satellite-detected fire activity. Users can draw or select an area on an interactive map, view the available MODIS and VIIRS observations from NASA FIRMS, and open a weekly calendar to compare activity across years. The calendar highlights weeks with unusual activity and shows the typical onset, peak, and end of the fire activity season.

MODIS and VIIRS have different spatial resolutions and detection capabilities. To make their records more comparable, FireLens groups hotspot detections into a common grid of H3 hexagonal cells and measures activity by counting the cells with at least one detection each day. It uses overlapping records from 2012 through 2021 to calibrate MODIS against VIIRS Suomi NPP for each area and month. The harmonized calendar uses Suomi NPP observations when available and labels estimates derived from calibrated MODIS data. The map displays observed detections, and the calendar distinguishes zero detections from missing sensor data. Hotspots indicate satellite detections that may warrant further investigation.

The central design choice was to pair a map of where hotspots were detected with a calendar of when activity changed. This lets researchers and land managers compare a recent week with the same time of year in previous years, identify periods that warrant closer investigation, and see which values are estimates when interpreting long-term patterns.

The interface uses TypeScript, React, MapLibre, and deck.gl. The API runs on Bun and Hono. Python and Polars process NASA FIRMS data. ClickHouse stores detections and daily grid aggregates, and PostgreSQL stores saved areas and ingestion records.
